answer: Every claim must carry a nadir seal, a signed record from a nearby beacon proving the filer was really there. The desk checks each seal against its registry within a day; a claim whose story mismatches its place is a fable, and each verified claim earns a drop of nectar for the next filing. Two distant beacons in an hour voids both claims and bars the identity a week. One honest person files from one place; a farm filing a thousand fakes needs a thousand real locations. One operator filed a hundred claims from one server room; every seal pointed to one beacon, and the desk voided them all.
